judged_text: Dead fallback in Google CalendarService.ts updateEvent (:254-257) and deleteEvent (:314-317): the `find()` predicate compares every calendar's externalId against a falsy `externalCalendarId`, so it can never match and the expression always evaluates to undefined; the previous `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` fallback is now dead code, so bookings whose calendar reference lacks externalCalendarId (legacy bookings plus new bookings created through the no-credentialId destination branch without externalId) update/delete against undefined or 'primary' via defaultCalendarId — leaving rescheduled Google events at the old time (external double-booking) and ghost events after cancellation

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` changed the fallback calendar selection to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. When `externalCalendarId` is `undefined`/`null` (which is plausible per this diff: `EventManager` now stores `externalCalendarId: result.externalId`, and many `createEvent(...)` calls pass no externalId, so `result.externalId` can be undefined), the predicate compares each `cal.externalId` to a falsy `externalCalendarId` and will not match any normal calendar entry, yielding `undefined`. That makes update/delete fall back to `primary` (or an undefined calendarId depending on downstream defaults), causing updates/deletes to target the wrong calendar and leaving the real event unchanged/undeleted.
